prompt: The function $h$ is defined by $h(x) = 5 - 2x$. If $h(a) = h(3) + 4$, what is the value of $a$?
hint: The right side contains only known numbers. Turn it into a single number before you do anything with $a$.

hints.text: The right side contains only known numbers. Turn it into a single number before you do anything with $a$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a smaller version: if $g(x) = 10 - x$ and $g(a) = g(2) + 3$, first get $g(2) = 8$, so $g(a) = 11$, giving $a = -1$. Always collapse the known side to a single number before solving.
Work out $h(3) = 5 - 2(3) = -1$, so the right side is $-1 + 4 = 3$. Now write $h(a)$ using the rule and set it equal to $3$.
Solving $5 - 2a = 3$ gives $-2a = -2$, so the value of $a$ is $1$.

learningObjective: Solve an equation involving function notation on both sides.
explanation: Evaluate the known side first, because it contains no unknown: $h(3) = 5 - 2(3) = -1$.
The equation now says $h(a) = -1 + 4 = 3$, which is a simple target for the function.
Replace $h(a)$ with the rule to get $5 - 2a = 3$. Subtracting $5$ gives $-2a = -2$, so $a = 1$.
A check confirms that $h(1) = 5 - 2 = 3$, so the value of $a$ is $1$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Use the slope directly
steps: The slope is $-2$: every step of $+1$ in $x$ drops the output by $2$.
You need an output $4$ higher than $h(3)$, so you must move $x$ down by $2$ steps.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Reading h(3) + 4 as h(3 + 4) = h(7) = −9 sends you solving the wrong equation entirely.
The +4 lives OUTSIDE the function: evaluate h(3) first, then add. Parentheses mark exactly what gets fed to the machine.
